source.title: Disentangling Steering Vectors
source.authors: Takeru Hiramatsu; Kyohei Atarashi; Koh Takeuchi; Hisashi Kashima

record.tranche_reason: The study uses a different method from the original: it extracts rejection-related SAE basis vectors from unsafe-minus-safe activation differences, removes a selected component from an unsafe DiffMean vector, and measures harmful-request responses.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the rejection-vector interpretations in Table 5 and StrongREJECT results in Tables 6 and 10. Semantic-consistency results for PubMedQA and other steering concepts do not measure refusal or harmful-request compliance and are not included. The paper does not test adding a rejection direction to induce refusals on harmless requests.
record.test_reason: The study never isolates or ablates a harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction in the model's activations. It builds an 'unsafe' steering vector from severity-3 minus safe PKU-SafeRLHF response-token activations. A 16-latent SAE splits that vector into parts, and LLM judges label some parts 'rejection'. The authors project one such part out of the steering vector and add the result at a single layer. The StrongREJECT scores therefore measure how well their edited steering vector works as a jailbreak, and the SVD comparison is method against method. Arditi et al. is cited only to motivate the experiment. 'Rejection' is a judge label that includes 'omits requested details', not a measured refusal direction. No version's mechanism (V1 ablation/addition, V4 refusal geometry in the model) is tested, so this is T4, with the finding recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors add that unedited unsafe DiffMean steering fails to raise compliance in 3 of 4 settings, which they attribute to rejection components cancelling the unsafe effect. They report the removal gain only for the earlier (0.5-depth) layers, and they note the decomposition is not canonical and depends on seed, data sample and latent dimensionality.
record.recipe_differences: Instead of finding and ablating the original single refusal direction across layers and positions, the study trains an SAE on paired activation differences, selects an interpreted rejection basis vector, subtracts its projection from an unsafe DiffMean vector, and evaluates the modified steering vector at one layer.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effect varies by intervention layer: the selected SAE component increases StrongREJECT scores at Qwen2.5 L13 and L20 and Llama3.1 L15, but not clearly at Llama3.1 L23. Results also vary by extraction method: SAE and SVD scores differ.

fits_no_version.finding: An unsafe-response DiffMean steering vector contains judge-labelled 'rejection' SAE components. Projecting one out raises StrongREJECT scores at Qwen2.5 L13 (0.018 to 0.352) and Llama3.1 L15 (0.015 to 0.084), slightly at Qwen L20, and not at Llama L23. Unedited DiffMean steering stays at or below the unsteered score in 3 of 4 settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Contrastive unsafe/safe steering vectors carry refusal-like components that counteract their jailbreak effect; removing those components makes steering more effective, mainly at mid-depth layers.

record.problems: Only two instruct models and two layers are tested. The paper relies on LLM judges for vector interpretation and selection, reports no human-annotated ground truth or inter-judge agreement, and notes that the decomposition depends on initialization, training data sample, and latent dimensionality. The harmfulness measure is StrongREJECT score, not a direct refusal-rate measure. General capabilities are not evaluated.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant refusal or harmful-compliance results left out. Semantic consistency and steering-shift results for other concepts are excluded because they do not measure refusal or harmful-request compliance.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction from harmful vs harmless instructions; no directional ablation in activations; no addition to induce refusal; no capability check.
No analysis of jailbreak mechanisms or adversarial training.
No analysis of refusal geometry in the model. The multiple 'rejection' latents come from a 16-latent SAE on unsafe-response differences.

missing.what: Second-seed StrongREJECT replication: Qwen L13 0.028/0.096/0.373; L20 0.031/0.023/0.037 (CI spans 0); Llama L15 0.016/0.032/0.106; L23 no rejection vector found.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and its V1/V4 labels are rejected. The study's intervention edits a steering vector rather than ablating a refusal direction in the model. Its rejection components are LLM-judge labels on a forced 16-latent decomposition of unsafe-response differences, so neither V1 nor V4 is measured. There is no human validation of the interpretations and no capability evaluation.

versions.untested_parts: Does not ablate a single original difference-in-means refusal direction at every layer and position; does not test adding the direction to induce refusals on harmless requests or measure preservation of general abilities.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
Does not test whether jailbreak attacks suppress the direction or whether training against ablation improves robustness.
Does not establish a canonical affine or cone geometry, or compare a dominant direction plus other directions across the full model.
No separate harmfulness-judgment versus refusal-decision measurement.
No cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer test; using two instruct models is not a transfer test.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: SAE rejection-component removal at Qwen2.5 L13 and L20 and Llama3.1 L15
reader_labels.reason: Removing a selected component raises StrongREJECT scores in these settings, but the study measures benchmark scores rather than refusal rates and the effect is not consistently a complete loss of refusal (r9, r12, r15). The L23 result is absent (r18).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SAE-extracted rejection-related components and their removal in the tested PKU-SafeRLHF settings
reader_labels.reason: The study identifies distinct rejection-related interpretations, including two at Qwen2.5 L13 and two at Llama3.1 L15; removing a selected component increases harmful-request benchmark scores in three of four model-layer settings (r1-r6, r9, r12, r15).
